conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. ___ . I understand you've been having pelvic pain. Can you tell me more about it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it's sharp pain on the left side, comes and goes. It’s been going on for three days now. Lasts about 20 seconds each time, then stops. It goes down to my rectum and into my left leg.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You mentioned this feels similar to past flares of your endometriosis?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. I’ve had this before. I tried naproxen and a heating pad, but nothing helped this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Your vitals have stabilized now, and your exam shows mild tenderness in the lower left abdomen, but no signs of infection or serious complications. We’ll run some tests to be sure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need surgery? I’m really worried it’s something worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No surgery planned. We did an ultrasound to check for ovarian issues like torsion or cysts, and everything looks normal. No free fluid, no blockages. This supports that it’s a flare of your known endometriosis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. That’s a relief. So what’s next?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to manage your pain with medications. You’ll get some Dilaudid now for immediate relief, and we’ll start you on gabapentin, ibuprofen, and Tylenol to help control the flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m on lithium already—will that be okay with the new meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, lithium is safe to continue. We’ve noted your allergies too—Reglan, erythromycin, and Effexor—so we’ll avoid those. The pain meds we’re giving are safe with your current regimen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How’s the pain today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better, actually. Not gone, but much more manageable. I slept a few hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Your labs came back normal—white blood cell count is fine, no sign of infection. Lactate was slightly elevated last night but not concerning, especially since you were in a lot of pain when it was drawn.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s definitely endometriosis and not something else?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Based on your history, exam, normal ultrasound, and labs, yes. There’s no sign of infection, pregnancy, or ovarian issues. This is consistent with an acute flare of your chronic condition.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done well overnight. We’re going to discharge you home today. You’ll continue gabapentin three times a day, ibuprofen every six hours as needed, and tramadol or Tylenol for breakthrough pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Should I watch for anything specific?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Call your doctor or come back if you develop a fever over 100.4, severe pain, heavy vaginal bleeding, trouble urinating, or nausea so bad you can’t keep meds down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And I have my follow-up with Dr. ___ next week?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly. We’ll send your records there. Keep taking care of yourself, and try to rest as much as possible over the next few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you so much. I feel much better than yesterday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’re glad we could help. You’re cleared to go home whenever you’re ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll get my things together then. Appreciate all the care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, and don’t hesitate to reach out if things change.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Have a good day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You too. See you at your follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks again.
